articles/atomic-original-directory-delet.title: Atomic original directory deletion | MirrorPulse Adapter SDK documentation
articles/atomic-original-directory-delet.summary: Atomic original directory deletion A backend that can commit a whole admitted subtree in one native transaction can offer atomic-original-directory-delete-v1, in addition to original-directory-admission-v1. This does not enable the separate individual child or final-directory effect capabilities. No default handshake enables it. DeleteOriginalDirectoryAtomically returns OriginalDirectoryDeletedAtomically; ordinary MutationComplete is insufficient. The request includes the complete original admission request and backend admission, and binds their fingerprints to the Host's sealed manifest. All operations must be conditional Delete operations in the admitted leaf-first order. Move, upload and directory creation are outside this capability. A staged cross-instance move may use this operation for source retirement only after the Host has durably verified the complete destination copy and authorized every source operation. The capability itself supplies no copy or verification proof. The backend revalidates its durable admission, complete inventory, original generations and conditions under the same qualified history and exclusion boundary as its native transaction. It reserves the immutable Host authorization before source mutation. The same admission or any of its operation IDs cannot be rebound to another plan, manifest or individual-effect execution. Capability negotiation, hashes and SDK shape checks cannot establish these native facts. All original removals and one immutable receipt commit together. No child result is returned or counted as accepted before the batch commits. The receipt retains every operation ID, original address and original generation in the authorized order, as well as the request, admission and manifest fingerprints and backend commit evidence. It is a whole-batch receipt; it is not a chain of provisional AdapterOwnedChildEffectReceipt values. It has no fabricated deletion revision. Before commit, cancellation or process death must preserve every original and leave no accepted receipt. After commit, a lost reply, cancellation or process restart must recover the identical receipt without opening or mutating a later occupant at the original path. The backend refuses changed authorization and missing, corrupt or incompatible retained evidence. Host acknowledgement follows durable acceptance of the full receipt and remains a separate product step. AdapterAtomicDirectoryDeletionWire checks protocol, both capabilities, request/session/instance correlation, a 1 MiB body limit and exact reply membership. The dispatcher validates before invoking IAdapterAtomicDirectoryDeletionBackend and validates its reply. Signed Host/Worker integration must separately qualify durability, native history/exclusion, root authorization and official journal ACK. The SDK contract checks use a synthetic backend and do not claim those outcomes.

articles/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | MirrorPulse Adapter SDK documentation
articles/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started A MirrorPulse Adapter runs as a Worker process. The public SDK provides the versioned protocol types and helps the Worker communicate with the MirrorPulse Host. One deployment describes one storage root. Build the sample and run the contract checks From the SDK repository root, use the .NET SDK version in global.json. dotnet restore MirrorPulse.Adapter.sln --locked-mode dotnet build MirrorPulse.Adapter.sln -c Release --no-restore dotnet run --project tests/MirrorPulse.Adapter.ContractTests -c Release --no-build The contract test executable exercises the wire contracts and launches the sample memory Worker. The memory Worker demonstrates the process boundary. A production Worker must declare only the capabilities its storage backend supports. Use the Adapter template when starting an independent Adapter. Keep runtime data and credentials under the Host's ownership. Build and sign a package with the template's release tooling before testing installation in MirrorPulse.

articles/original-directory-admission-wi.title: Original directory admission and child effects | MirrorPulse Adapter SDK documentation
articles/original-directory-admission-wi.summary: Original directory admission and child effects A Worker negotiates original-directory-admission-v1 before accepting AdmitOriginalDirectory, which returns OriginalDirectoryAdmitted. Individual ApplyOriginalChild / OriginalChildApplied exchanges additionally require original-directory-effects-v1 and original-directory-child-effects-v1. The existing RetireOriginalDirectory message completes an admitted directory after its children under its existing effects capability. Admission alone grants neither mutation path. The Host sends the original instance, admission ID and complete ordered source operations. Every entry retains its stable operation ID, address, explicit revision condition, destination for a move and absence condition. Children precede their direct parent and all paths form one connected subtree. Move destinations leave that original subtree. The request fingerprint covers the entire ordered plan. The plan has at most 2048 operations. The backend checks its complete inventory and original conditions and persists the admission before replying. The reply binds each operation to its original generation, a directory witness where appropriate and the exact source and destination parent witnesses. Witnesses retain the admission request fingerprint. The admission fingerprint covers those observations. Duplicate requests recover that same admission. A changed request or incomplete inventory is refused. The backend retains the stable operation claims across admissions. Each file effect request retains the admission and Host manifest fingerprints, original operation and generation, original parent witnesses and the previously accepted receipt for each affected parent. Its fingerprint includes these bindings. The backend validates the request against its durable admission and checks each predecessor against its accepted effect ledger. Shape validation by itself cannot establish those backend facts. The backend binds the Host manifest once per admission and requires the same binding for every child effect and final directory retirement. The typed child receipt binds the full request fingerprint, original generation and exact before/after transitions for each original parent. The first effect starts from the admitted revision. Later effects extend the previously accepted receipt. A deletion's accepted revision is null. The backend commits the native effect and durable receipt together and returns that receipt after a lost reply or process restart. The Host persists the same receipt before advancing its plan. AdapterOriginalDirectoryWire validates protocol, negotiated capabilities, bounded payloads and request/session/instance correlation. Each body is limited to 1 MiB. AdapterOriginalDirectoryDispatcher decodes before calling the backend and validates the backend reply before returning a control frame. A Worker can route these messages from its existing control reader to an IAdapterOriginalDirectoryBackend implementation. An admission-only backend can implement IAdapterOriginalDirectoryAdmissionBackend; the dispatcher refuses individual effects when that implementation is unavailable. Backend implementations also own root authorization, native path rules, complete history, exclusion during validation and mutation, and crash recovery. The dispatcher supports protocol validation around that implementation. Production enablement requires signed Host and Worker qualification of the complete admitted operation and official journal acknowledgement. A backend that only commits an entire original subtree atomically can use the separately negotiated atomic deletion contract. It must not return an individual child receipt while that child's native transaction can still roll back.

articles/original-directory-retirement-w.title: Original directory retirement messages | MirrorPulse Adapter SDK documentation
articles/original-directory-retirement-w.summary: Original directory retirement messages This optional draft extends the original-directory evidence types with a typed protocol-v2 request and response boundary. It does not implement a backend, enable a capability in the default handshake, or authorize journal ACK. The shipping sample Worker remains unsupported for these messages. The negotiated capability is original-directory-effects-v1. The new request message is RetireOriginalDirectory; its successful response message is OriginalDirectoryRetired. Ordinary Delete, Move and MutationComplete messages cannot stand in for these messages. Protocol 1, absent capability, unknown versions and differently cased capability names are refused. Request AdapterDirectoryRetirementRequest contains the final nonrecursive Delete or Move of one original directory. It retains: The immutable operation ID, exact source address, destination for a move, and explicit source revision precondition. The complete AdapterDirectoryRetirementEvidence: original directory witness, sealed manifest fingerprint, required direct-child operations, chronologically accepted child receipts and the terminal owned directory revision. The exact original source and destination direct-parent witnesses. The source parent's generation must equal the admitted directory's parent generation. Each available original parent predecessor receipt, separately from the child ledger. One parent may have at most one predecessor; a receipt that affects both parents may be supplied once. No foreign, duplicate or unrelated receipt can become the basis of a new parent transition. A canonical SHA-256 fingerprint of all these fields. Required-child set and parent ordering are canonical; accepted-child chronology remains significant. The source precondition must equal the child ledger's final expected revision. It cannot be absent, replaced by a current Stat, or silently taken from a later object. The final operation cannot reuse a child operation ID. The source cannot be a configured root; a move cannot replace a destination, target a configured root, or move into its own subtree. Backends must additionally apply their native path normalization and alias rules. An author constructs the retained request and uses CalculateFingerprint() to bind it. Every decoder revalidates the complete request. Recalculating a hash is not permission to rebase retained state or replace an original child manifest. Witness provenance and sealed-manifest ownership remain backend/Host duties. Response and recovery The response payload is the existing AdapterOwnedChildEffectReceipt, with the exact request fingerprint, operation, admission, instance, original directory generation, source and destination. It must contain precisely the admitted direct-parent transitions. Each transition extends the retained predecessor; without a predecessor it starts at the original parent revision and has no predecessor fingerprint. A deletion's accepted revision remains null. AdapterDirectoryRetirementWire.ReadRequest and ReadResponse validate the payload and envelope. Responses must match the request ID, Worker session, instance, protocol and response role. Each payload is limited to 1 MiB, below the existing outer frame limit. A null or ordinary mutation response is not evidence of retirement. These checks grant no native mutation authority. A capable backend still needs to verify original identity/history and the complete child manifest under its atomicity or exclusion mechanism; commit effects and durable receipts together; and recover a lost reply without touching a later tree. The Host must persist and compare the exact receipt before advancing its ledger or acknowledging an original journal operation. Unsupported backends leave the original pending. The bounded request does not introduce manifest paging; an oversized admission requires explicit refusal rather than truncation. The contract executable exercises encoded control-frame round trips, complete child chains, exact parent predecessors, Delete and cross-root Move responses, null revisions, changed bindings, replay-correlation mistakes, downgrade and payload limits. These are SDK wire-boundary checks, not a claim that a live Worker/backend or recursive Host acceptance is complete.

articles/package-configuration.html.summary: Package configuration contract SDK 1.0 packages use manifest schema 2. Keep one rootDefinitions item and set instancePolicy.maximumRootDefinitions to 1. One Adapter package can still be installed in multiple deployments. Use a canonical lowercase Adapter ID and a three-part stable or -preview.N package version. Use presentation for the package title, description, logo, and form. These are separate from the stable Adapter ID. { "presentation": { "titleKey": "package.title", "descriptionKey": "package.description", "logoPath": "assets/logo.png", "formPath": "forms/config.xml" }, "locales": ["en-US"], "localeMetadata": { "en-US": { "displayName": "English (United States)", "resourcePath": "locales/en-US.json" } } } Include each referenced file in the signed package inventory, with the exact same spelling and case. Resource paths use / and are relative to the package root. Images use PNG, JPEG, ICO or BMP. Locale files are flat JSON objects that map label keys to display text. The en-US table covers every label used in the form and presentation. A selected locale can omit keys to use the corresponding English text. The separate form is declarative XML. Its supported layout items are heading, paragraph and image. Every image requires a localized accessibility label. Field keys remain stable across releases. The form also supports the following editable controls and callback buttons. <form version="1"> <heading textKey="setup.title" /> <paragraph textKey="setup.instructions" /> <image path="assets/logo.png" altKey="package.title" /> <text key="endpoint" labelKey="field.endpoint" required="true" /> <password key="accessToken" labelKey="field.accessToken" required="false" /> <singleChoice key="mode" labelKey="field.mode" required="true" default="read"> <option id="read" labelKey="mode.read" /> <option id="write" labelKey="mode.write" /> </singleChoice> <multiChoice key="scopes" labelKey="field.scopes" required="false" default="read,write"> <option id="read" labelKey="mode.read" /> <option id="write" labelKey="mode.write" /> </multiChoice> <checkBox key="enabled" labelKey="field.enabled" required="false" default="true" /> <callback id="authorize" labelKey="action.authorize"> <write key="accessToken" /> <write key="scopes" /> </callback> </form> Use stable field keys, option IDs, and callback IDs independent of display language. The form requires a true or false value for each field's required attribute. Defaults are optional. Password fields cannot declare defaults. A single choice default names one option ID. Multiple choice defaults use comma-separated IDs and an empty default selects nothing. Check box defaults are true or false. AdapterPackageMetadata.Read validates the versioned package metadata against the signed file inventory. AdapterConfigurationForm.Read validates the layout, field bindings and callback write declarations. AdapterConfigurationTranslations.Read verifies the fallback string table and resolves display labels. These methods operate on parsed metadata and package data supplied by the caller. The Host validates the signature and continues to own configuration, authorization transactions, validation and persistence. A callback's write list is the maximum set of fields the Host may accept from that callback. Authorization, health and updates Configuration-only Worker startup MirrorPulse can start the signed Worker before any deployment exists and can use the same mode to reauthorize an existing deployment. Parse the usual AdapterWorkerProcessArguments and inspect ConfigurationOnly. In that mode, advertise AdapterConfigurationCallbackContract.Capability with protocol 2, then validate the Host's Ready with that launch mode. The accepted Ready has zero root bindings and includes the settings available for this authorization. Keep the normal sync handshake and startup path when ConfigurationOnly is false. var arguments = AdapterWorkerProcessArguments.Parse(args); var offer = new AdapterHello(new(2, 2), arguments.ConfigurationOnly ? [AdapterConfigurationCallbackContract.Capability] : AdapterHandshake.V2Capabilities); // Send Hello and decode its matching Ready response as AdapterReady. AdapterHandshake.ValidateReady(ready, offer, arguments.ConfigurationOnly); channel.SelectProtocol(ready.SelectedVersion); In configuration-only mode, handle ConfigurationCallbackStart, ConfigurationCallbackPoll, ConfigurationCallbackCancel, and the Host's Stop. Read callback messages with AdapterConfigurationCallbackContract.ReadRequest after reading the frame from AdapterControlChannel. Track the invocation ID, callback ID and expiry in memory for this session. Send ConfigurationCallbackResult as a response with the matching frame request ID. A pending response can include an HTTPS authorization page. A Worker that owns its own interaction window can return pending without a URL. A successful response proposes values only for fields listed in the callback's signed write list. Cancel ends the interaction and discards proposed writes. AdapterReady.CredentialBindings indexes opaque Host credential references by password field key. For an existing deployment, a Worker can use a supplied reference with a CredentialRequest and read its matching CredentialResponse on the authenticated channel. Password values stay out of ordinary configuration and logs. Use the temporary cache directories supplied by the Host and keep authorization state in memory. MirrorPulse accepts authorized writes when the user saves the form, stores passwords in its credential store and ends the temporary Worker session. Send file operations, directory state and change notifications from the normal sync session. Health and updates Offer AdapterDeploymentContract.StructuredHealthCapability when the Worker can identify configuration and credential issues. If the ordinary deployment's Ready selects that capability, send the complete AdapterHealthReport as a protocol 2 notification with AdapterDeploymentContract.HealthReportMessage, a fresh frame request ID, and isResponse: false. It can arrive before Connected when a credential blocks startup. Replace the report as conditions change, and send an empty issue list after recovery. Include the exact signed form field key when known. Credential issues can name password fields. Source and Worker failures carry no field. Keep the report within 16 unique issues and keep arbitrary diagnostic text and credential values out of it. Update checks are optional. A Worker can include update-discovery in its protocol 2 Hello and check that Ready selects it. After Connected, the Host can send CheckAdapterUpdate with an empty object. Reply with AdapterUpdateOffer using the same request, instance and session identifiers. This exchange applies to the selected deployment and carries no rootKey. Serialize AdapterPackageUpdateResult as the response payload. Set Offer to null when the selected package is current. Otherwise, offer the same Adapter ID, a strictly newer version, and an HTTPS URL or the absolute path of a local Windows .mpadapter file, represented as a file: URI. HTTPS packages carry an embedded signature. The Host asks the user before acquiring the package and checks its signature and identity before registering the version. Users can then select that version for each deployment.

index.html.summary: How to build an Adapter MirrorPulse Adapter SDK provides the public Worker API, wire protocol specification, and conformance tools for MirrorPulse Adapters. Start with the Adapter template. Read the Worker protocol for package and wire contracts. Use the sample Worker and conformance tool to validate an implementation. The 1.0 development baseline targets one declared root per Adapter deployment.
